views.name: crime_events_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  case_number,
  date AS event_timestamp,
  SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64) AS event_year,
  block,
  iucr,
  primary_type,
  description,
  location_description,
  arrest,
  domestic,
  beat,
  district,
  ward,
  community_area,
  fbi_code,
  x_coordinate,
  y_coordinate,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  location
FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
grain: unique_key (one row per reported crime incident)
views.description: Normalized, cleaned projection of the crime table preserving identifiers, timestamps, location and key attributes. Use as a base for aggregations, joins, and time-series analyses of crimes. | Use for: Counts of crimes by time period or area; Filtering crimes by type/attribute and joining to other datasets; Spatial analyses using crime latitude/longitude

views.name: crime_counts_by_day_type
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(event_timestamp) AS day,
  primary_type,
  community_area,
  district,
  COUNT(1) AS crimes_count
FROM (
  SELECT
    date AS event_timestamp,
    primary_type,
    community_area,
    district
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
)
GROUP BY day, primary_type, community_area, district
grain: day, primary_type, community_area, district (one row per combination)
views.description: Daily counts of crimes grouped by date (day) and primary type, preserving community area and district for downstream joins and ranking. Useful for time series, trend detection and top-k by day/type. | Use for: Daily trend of crime counts by type and area; Top crime types per community area or district on a given day (use a rank CTE on top); Moving averages or seasonality analyses at daily granularity

views.name: taxi_trips_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  taxi_id,
  trip_start_timestamp AS start_ts,
  trip_end_timestamp AS end_ts,
  trip_seconds,
  trip_miles,
  pickup_census_tract,
  dropoff_census_tract,
  pickup_community_area,
  dropoff_community_area,
  fare,
  tips,
  tolls,
  extras,
  trip_total,
  payment_type,
  company,
  pickup_latitude,
  pickup_longitude,
  pickup_location,
  dropoff_latitude,
  dropoff_longitude,
  dropoff_location
FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
views.description: Cleaned projection of taxi trips preserving identifiers, timestamps, fares, distances and pickup/dropoff areas and coordinates. Use as a canonical base for trip-level analyses and downstream aggregations or joins. | Use for: Average fare, tips, or trip distance by company or payment type; Time-series of trip counts or revenue; Spatial analyses of pickups/dropoffs by community area

views.name: taxi_daily_agg_by_company
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(trip_start_timestamp) AS day,
  company,
  COUNT(1) AS trips_count,
  SUM(IFNULL(trip_total, 0)) AS total_revenue,
  SUM(IFNULL(fare, 0)) AS total_fare,
  SUM(IFNULL(tips, 0)) AS total_tips,
  AVG(IFNULL(trip_miles, 0)) AS avg_miles,
  AVG(IFNULL(trip_seconds, 0)) AS avg_seconds
FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
GROUP BY day, company
grain: day, company (one row per company per day)
views.description: Daily aggregated metrics per taxi company (or NULL for missing company) including counts, sums and averages for fare, tips, trip_miles and trip_seconds. Useful for revenue/time trend comparisons and ranking companies. | Use for: Rank companies by revenue or trips over time; Compare tipping behavior across companies or days; Compute moving averages or growth rates of company revenue

views.name: crime_to_pickup_area_joinable
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS crime_id,
  DATE(date) AS crime_day,
  primary_type,
  community_area AS crime_community_area,
  district,
  latitude AS crime_latitude,
  longitude AS crime_longitude
FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
views.description: Joinable relation projecting crime records keyed by community_area and date to enable safe aggregation joins with taxi trips by pickup_community_area and day. Designed to be aggregated further to avoid row explosion when joining two event tables. | Use for: Aggregate join with taxi daily pickups by community area and day (e.g., compare counts); Spatial proximity joins using crime_latitude/longitude to pickup coordinates; Time-windowed correlation of crime counts vs taxi activity

views.name: taxi_pickups_by_day_area
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(trip_start_timestamp) AS day,
  pickup_community_area,
  COUNT(1) AS trips_count,
  SUM(IFNULL(trip_total, 0)) AS total_revenue,
  AVG(IFNULL(trip_miles, 0)) AS avg_miles
FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
GROUP BY day, pickup_community_area
grain: day, pickup_community_area (one row per area per day)
views.description: Daily counts and sums of taxi pickups aggregated by pickup community area, preserving day and area to join with crime aggregates. Keeps measures useful for normalization (trips_count, total_revenue). | Use for: Compare daily taxi activity to daily crime counts by community area; Compute ratios like crimes per taxi trip in an area/day; Identify area-days with unusually high taxi revenue or trip counts

views.name: top_crime_types_by_area_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  day,
  primary_type,
  community_area,
  crimes_count,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY day, community_area ORDER BY crimes_count DESC) AS type_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    DATE(date) AS day,
    primary_type,
    community_area,
    COUNT(1) AS crimes_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
  GROUP BY day, primary_type, community_area
)
grain: day, community_area, primary_type (one row per type per area per day)
views.description: Pre-ranked crime type counts by community area and day. Exposes a rank column so downstream queries can select top-N crime types per area/day by filtering rank <= N. Useful for top-k and leaderboard queries. | Use for: Top N crime types per community area on a given day or date range; Leaderboards of crime types for dashboards (use WHERE type_rank <= N)

views.name: taxi_company_revenue_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  day,
  company,
  trips_count,
  total_revenue,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY day ORDER BY total_revenue DESC) AS revenue_rank
FROM (
  SELECT
    DATE(trip_start_timestamp) AS day,
    company,
    COUNT(1) AS trips_count,
    SUM(IFNULL(trip_total, 0)) AS total_revenue
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
  GROUP BY day, company
)
grain: day, company (one row per company per day)
views.description: Ranked daily revenue per taxi company. Provides company daily revenue and rank within each day so consumers can easily filter top companies by revenue for any day. | Use for: Top-N companies by revenue for dashboard daily snapshots; Time-series of rank changes for companies

views.name: crime_events_weekly_running_total
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  day,
  primary_type,
  community_area,
  crimes_count,
  SUM(crimes_count) OVER (
    PARTITION BY primary_type, community_area
    ORDER BY day
    ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS running_7day_crimes
FROM (
  SELECT
    DATE(date) AS day,
    primary_type,
    community_area,
    COUNT(1) AS crimes_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
  GROUP BY day, primary_type, community_area
)
ORDER BY primary_type, community_area, day
grain: day, primary_type, community_area (one row per group per day)
views.description: 7-day running total of crimes per primary_type and community_area using event date. Useful for smoothing daily volatility and detecting trends. Exposes running_total so downstream queries can filter or chart moving sums. | Use for: Trend detection using 7-day moving sums; Comparing recent crime activity across areas or types

views.name: distinct_crime_types
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  primary_type,
  COUNT(1) AS sample_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
GROUP BY primary_type
ORDER BY primary_type
views.description: Distinct list of crime primary types and their sample counts. Useful for enumeration, filtering UIs, and semantic lists of available categories. | Use for: Populate dropdowns of crime types; Quick checks of category cardinality

views.name: distinct_taxi_companies
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  company,
  COUNT(1) AS trips_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
GROUP BY company
ORDER BY company
views.description: Distinct list of taxi companies with counts of trips. Useful for UI lists and quick popularity measures. | Use for: Populate company filters in dashboards; Assess company coverage in dataset

views.name: spatial_nearest_taxi_pickups
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS trip_id,
  taxi_id,
  pickup_latitude,
  pickup_longitude,
  pickup_location,
  pickup_community_area,
  DATE(trip_start_timestamp) AS pickup_day,
  trip_total,
  trip_miles
FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
WHERE pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL AND pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
grain: trip_id (one row per taxi trip with non-null pickup coordinates)
views.description: For each crime event (with latitude/longitude), returns the N nearest taxi pickup locations within a configurable neighborhood when joined with taxi trips aggregated by pickup location. This CTE projects pickup coordinates and preserves taxi identifiers so consumers can perform distance calculations or nearest-neighbor joins downstream. Note: this CTE does not perform the spatial join itself to avoid explosion; it prepares taxi pickup locations for downstream spatial joins using ST_DISTANCE or haversine. | Use for: Spatial nearest-neighbor joins between crimes and taxi pickups; Compute distances from crimes to nearest taxi pickups and analyze temporal proximity

views.name: crime_latest_by_case
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key,
  case_number,
  date,
  primary_type,
  description,
  location_description,
  arrest,
  domestic,
  updated_on,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY case_number ORDER BY updated_on DESC) AS rn
FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
grain: case_number, rn (one row per case_number per version; rn=1 is latest)
views.description: Latest crime record per case_number using updated_on as the versioning column. Exposes a row_number so downstream consumers can select the most recent record per case_number. Useful when case_number may have multiple updates. | Use for: Select the latest record per case_number for deduplication; Auditing or change-tracking workflows that need the most recent incident data
